interest: For historians, this file provides significant insight into the pre-war and wartime intersection of scientific conservation, intelligence gathering, and national security policy regarding Japanese maritime activities. It highlights how scientific research into Alaskan salmon migrations in Bristol Bay—originally initiated by the Fish and Wildlife Service to provide the State Department with data to counter Japanese commercial encroachment—was disrupted by military mobilizations and the outbreak of hostilities. The file also illustrates the hemispheric reach of American and Allied security vigilance against Japanese fishing fleets, detailing intelligence monitoring and rapid internment actions in Baja California, Mexico, as well as port controls, citizenship revocations, and operational restrictions on Japanese-descended fishermen in Santos, Brazil. Finally, the inclusion of Yale Civil Affairs Training School correspondence demonstrates how the U.S. government incorporated fisheries expertise into its planning for the post-surrender military occupation and economic administration of Japan.
overview: This file from State Department decimal file 894.628 (Animal Husbandry, Japan: Fisheries) covers records from August 1940 through December 1944 relating to Japanese fisheries, fishing vessels, and related wartime security and postwar planning. It includes interdepartmental correspondence and an extensive 1942 scientific report from the Department of the Interior's Fish and Wildlife Service on salmon resources and migrations in Bristol Bay and the Bering Sea, an investigation initially launched to assess Japanese fishing encroachment in Alaskan waters before being curtailed by World War II. The file also documents diplomatic, naval, and consular surveillance of Japanese fishing vessels, floating crab canneries, and trawlers across the Western Hemisphere, including sightings off Alaska, legal actions in Honolulu, Mexican seizures and internment of Japanese vessels and crews off Lower California following Pearl Harbor, and stringent security restrictions and citizenship revocations imposed on Japanese fishermen in Santos, Brazil. In addition, the file contains correspondence from Yale University's Civil Affairs Training School inviting State Department fisheries experts to lecture officers preparing for the military occupation and civil administration of postwar Japan.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an excerpt from the Alaska Fishery Investigations Report for Fiscal Year 1942 concerning Bristol Bay salmon resources.
subfiles.summary: Acting Director J. Clark Salyer II of the Fish and Wildlife Service transmits to Leo D. Sturgeon in the Department of State an excerpt from the Alaska Fishery Investigations Report for Fiscal Year 1942. The material is provided in response to Sturgeon's letter of May 15 addressed to Assistant Director Charles E. Jackson. Salyer conveys his hope that the enclosed survey data on Bristol Bay salmon will prove useful to the State Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Clark Salyer II to Leo D. Sturgeon

subfiles.about: Scientific investigations of the red salmon populations, oceanography, offshore migration routes, and inshore river escapements in Bristol Bay and the Bering Sea.
subfiles.from: Fish and Wildlife Service, Department of the Interior
subfiles.summary: This excerpt from the Fiscal Year 1942 Alaska Fishery Investigations Report reviews biological research on the red salmon resources of Bristol Bay. It covers oceanographic surveys conducted with the Coast Guard vessel Redwing, offshore experimental gillnetting along the Aleutian chain using the chartered vessel American Star, and inshore surveys of adult spawning escapement and fingerling migration across five major river systems. The offshore findings revealed that red salmon inhabit the continental shelf broadly and migrate through passes west of Unimak, contradicting earlier migration assumptions. Operations were suspended for the duration of the war due to military call-ups of personnel and the vicinity of active combat zones.
subfiles.title: Excerpt from Alaska Fishery Investigations Report for Fiscal Year 1942 on Bristol Bay Salmon Resources

subfiles.about: Request for reports and data on the Bristol Bay salmon fishery survey initiated to address Japanese fishing operations in Alaskan waters.
subfiles.summary: Leo D. Sturgeon of the Department of State writes to Charles E. Jackson, Assistant Director of the Fish and Wildlife Service, requesting available reports on the Bristol Bay salmon fishery survey begun in 1938. Sturgeon notes that the survey was originally instituted to collect data required by the State Department in connection with Japanese fishing operations in Alaskan waters. The material is requested to assist the Department in its current attention to problems involving coastal fisheries.
subfiles.title: Letter from Leo D. Sturgeon to Charles E. Jackson

subfiles.title: File transfer slip for 894.628/243a and 243b

subfiles.about: State Department charge slip charging file 894.628 materials to the office of Assistant Secretary Breckinridge Long.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State charge slip documenting that enclosure material from file 894.628 was charged to A-L (the office of Assistant Secretary Breckinridge Long) on December 24, 1941. The entry was handled by clerk JC and notes associated item 565.
subfiles.title: Charge slip for file 894.628

subfiles.about: Strictly confidential instruction requesting reports on renewed Japanese fishing boat activity off the west coast of Lower California.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State dispatches a strictly confidential air mail instruction to the American Consular Officer in charge at Guaymas, Sonora, Mexico. The instruction conveys reports of renewed operations by Japanese fishing vessels on the west coast of Lower California. The consular officer is directed to investigate and report promptly by air mail any pertinent information regarding these activities.
subfiles.title: Instruction to American Consular Officer, Guaymas, on Japanese fishing boats
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in charge, Guaymas, Sonora, Mexico

subfiles.about: Invitation to lecture officers at Yale University's Civil Affairs Training School on Japanese fishing and fisheries.
subfiles.summary: A. Whitney Griswold, Director of the Civil Affairs Training School at Yale University, writes to Leo D. Sturgeon inviting him to deliver a lecture on Japanese fisheries. Griswold explains that officers in the six-month program are preparing for civil affairs and military government responsibilities in occupied Japan. He mentions that Frank Williams of the State Department and Wolf I. Ladejinski of the Department of Agriculture are delivering companion lectures on the Japanese economy.
subfiles.title: Letter from A. Whitney Griswold to Leo D. Sturgeon

subfiles.about: Follow-up invitation to lecture at Yale's Civil Affairs Training School before January 22, 1945, with notation of Sturgeon's declination.
subfiles.summary: A. Whitney Griswold writes a follow-up letter to Leo D. Sturgeon urging him to address the Civil Affairs Training School at Yale before the conclusion of the term on January 22. Griswold emphasizes the vital importance of the fishing industry to the students' military government training. An administrative endorsement on the letter notes that on January 6, 1945, Sturgeon wired Griswold that he would be unable to travel to Yale.
subfiles.title: Letter from A. Whitney Griswold to Leo D. Sturgeon with reply note

subfiles.about: Intelligence report regarding Japanese floating crab cannery ship Kosei Maru and its fishing fleet anchored in the Bering Sea off Alaska.
subfiles.from: Division of International Communications, Department of State
subfiles.summary: A memorandum from the Division of International Communications informs Under Secretary of State Sumner Welles of a Coast Guard intelligence report received from the cutter Shoshone. The report states that the Japanese floating crab cannery ship Kosei Maru was anchored in the Bering Sea at 58° 36' N, 168° 48' W accompanied by nine 100-ton fishing vessels. The flotilla appeared fully outfitted and supplied for a prolonged stay in Alaskan waters.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for Under Secretary Welles on Japanese floating cannery Kosei Maru

subfiles.about: Naval intelligence report regarding Japanese fishing vessels and trawlers operating in Bristol Bay, Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Captain H. F. Kingman, Office of Naval Intelligence, transmits a confidential memorandum to Fletcher Warren of the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs. Kingman relays a Seattle District Intelligence Officer teletype indicating that Coast Guard sources observed Japanese fishing vessels operating in Bristol Bay. The ships included the Kosei Maru with eight steel tenders and one wooden tender, as well as the trawlers Suruga Maru and Tenyo Maru engaged in bottom fishing.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Captain H. F. Kingman to Fletcher Warren on Japanese vessels in Bristol Bay

subfiles.about: Transmittal of Honolulu customs investigative reports regarding court cases against Japanese fishing vessels for navigation law violations.
subfiles.summary: Mr. Rose of the Treasury Department forwards ten investigative reports from Customs Agents in Honolulu to Mr. Saugstad in the State Department on behalf of Assistant Secretary Herbert E. Gaston. The reports concern cases pending in the U.S. District Court and U.S. Attorney's office in Honolulu against Japanese fishing vessels for alleged violations of Section 4189 of the Revised Statutes (46 U.S.C. 60). A related letter from Commander Field of the Department of Commerce is also enclosed.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Mr. Rose to Francis M. Saugstad on Honolulu customs cases

subfiles.about: Paraphrase of naval intelligence report regarding the seizure of Japanese fishing vessels Yoshino and Ryono by Mexican authorities.
subfiles.summary: A strictly confidential paraphrase of a naval intelligence report received from the U.S. Naval Attaché in Mexico City on December 12, 1941. It quotes the American Consul at La Paz reporting that the Mexican government seized the Japanese fishing vessels Yoshino and Ryono at Cape San Lucas on December 9, 1941. The vessels were taken to San José del Cabo, and the crew members were transferred to La Paz for wartime internment.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of report from Naval Attaché, Mexico City, on Mexican seizure of Japanese fishing vessels

subfiles.about: Transmittal of Assistant Naval Attaché memorandum regarding Japanese fishing boats operating from Santos, Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Counselor of Embassy John F. Simmons transmits Despatch No. 8342 from Rio de Janeiro to the Secretary of State. The despatch encloses an intelligence memorandum prepared by Assistant Naval Attaché C. A. Crocker regarding Japanese fishing boats operating from the port of Santos. The document was forwarded by air mail and reviewed by Assistant Secretary Breckinridge Long's office.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 8342 from John F. Simmons on Japanese fishing boats operating from Santos

subfiles.about: Summary of Brazilian security measures, port restrictions, and citizenship revocations affecting Japanese fishermen operating out of Santos, Brazil.
keywords: Colonia de Pescadores Z-1 José Bonifácio
subfiles.summary: Assistant Naval Attaché C. A. Crocker reviews intelligence and security measures regarding Japanese fishing craft operating from Santos. Following a December 1941 letter from Rear Admiral A. T. Beauregard to Brazilian Vice Admiral Américo Vieira de Mello urging heightened harbor protection for Allied shipping, Brazilian authorities investigated 42 vessels in the Colonia de Pescadores Z-1 José Bonifácio owned by Japanese immigrants. Authorities moved to cancel the Brazilian citizenship of naturalized Japanese fishermen, restricted boats to a 12-mile radius and 36-hour trips, instituted mandatory departure permits and searches at Ponta da Praia, and ultimately barred Japanese-born and naturalized fishermen from going to sea.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by C. A. Crocker on Japanese fishing boats operating from Santos, Brazil
